newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals steady, dlr firms in Asia.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals steady, dlr firms in Asia.

text.p: * Rupiah stable ahead of economic data this week
* Dollar/ringgit steady, exporter sales just above 2.4950
* Dollar/Sing bears run out of steam, but upside limited by large U.S. buy-orders at 1.4060
* Thai baht weaker on dollar rise versus majors but tight liquidity hampers dollar-gains
The Malaysian ringgit traded in a tight band against the dollar on Tuesday and is expected to keep within its suffocating range today.
"On a daily basis, we'd be lucky now to get a 10-pointer movement," said a senior dealer at a local bank in Malaysia.
The Malaysian currency was maintaining a soft bias with the dollar well supported against the majors due to heightened Iraq/U.S. tensions, dealers said.
But they said dollar gains intraday would be capped by Malaysian exporter sales just above the 2.4950 ringgit level.
At 0515 GMT, the ringgit was trading at 2.4942/47 to the dollar.

In Indonesia, the rupiah also tracked a confined range ahead of the release of economic indicators later this week and the upcoming hearing for the court case between deposed opposition leader Megawati Sukarnoputri and the Indonesian government.
"The market remains quiet and featureless. Some Singapore operators were seen buying dollars, but they failed to have much impact on the market," one European bank dealer said.
"Operators prefer staying on the sidelines and waiting for the latest economic figures such as inflation," he said.
Dealers said dollar/rupiah rates were likely to stay little changed later today on the lack of fresh leads.
Spot rupiah was last at 2,343.0/43.25, compared with an opening of 2,342.50/43.00.
The central bank set its intervention rate at 2,341/2,459 and the conversion rate at 2,341/2,387 on Monday.
In Thailand, the dollar gained against the baht on the back of its strength against the majors, but tight domestic liquidity was likely to cap near-term dollar gains, dealers said.
Dealers said the money supply would be tight for the rest of the week as a result of bimonthly corporate tax payment and the coming reserve requirement.
All commercial banks have to meet the central bank's reserve requirement on the seventh and 22nd of every month.
The one-month dollar/baht swap premium rose to 8.25/9.25 satangs per a dollar early from 7.30/7.80 late on Monday on tight money supply, dealers said.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the mid-rate at 25.32 to the dollar against 25.31 on Monday.
Spot dollar-baht was trading at 25.312/315 at 0515 GMT.
The Singapore dollar was banded in tight trade but dealers said dollar-Sing bears may be running out of steam.
But upside for the Singapore unit is capped in the near-term at 1.4060 by large U.S. buy orders, some market players said.
- Reme Ahmad in Kuala Lumpur (603-230-8911), Tang Nguyen in Bangkok (662-252-9950), Valerie Lee in Singapore (65-870-3080)
